items.q: Glomerular filtration rate is defined as the amount of urine filtered by:
opts: All the nephrons in both kidneys in one minute
All nephrons of one kidney in one hour
The glomerular capillaries in one second
items.exp: Definition: amount of urine filtered by all the nephrons in both kidneys in one minute. (Book p734)

items.q: Fill up: GFR = net ultrafiltration pressure × the ultrafiltration (UF) ______.
items.exp: GFR = net ultrafiltration pressure × ultrafiltration (UF) coefficient. (Book p734)

items.q: Match each Starling pressure of the glomerulus with its book value — 1) Glomerular hydrostatic pressure 2) Bowman's capsule pressure 3) Glomerular colloid osmotic pressure … A) 32 mm Hg B) 60 mm Hg C) 18 mm Hg
items.exp: Glomerular hydrostatic 60 mm Hg; Bowman's capsule 18 mm Hg; glomerular colloid osmotic 32 mm Hg. (Book p734)

items.q: The net filtration pressure worked out in the book's boxes is:
items.exp: Net filtration pressure (10 mm Hg) = glomerular hydrostatic (60) − Bowman's capsule (18) − glomerular oncotic (32). (Book p734)

items.q: Using [(60 − 18) − (32 − 0)] × 12.5 ml/min/mmHg, the book's calculated GFR is:
Fill up: In the expansion of the oncotic term, the Bowman's space oncotic pressure is taken as ______.
items.exp: (Glomerular capillary OP − Bowman's space OP) uses Bowman's space OP = 0. (Book p734)

items.q: Which of the following statements about the GFR calculation is TRUE?
opts: The UF coefficient is subtracted from the net pressure
Bowman's capsule pressure adds to filtration
Net ultrafiltration pressure = net hydrostatic pressure minus net oncotic pressure
Net ultrafiltration pressure = net oncotic pressure minus net hydrostatic pressure
items.exp: GFR = [net hydrostatic pressure (H.P) − net oncotic pressure (O.P)] × UF coefficient. (Book p734)
